'''Team Albany''' is a Star Wars CCG playtest team from Albany, New York (Decipher's Coruscant region). [[Matt Sokol]] is a founding member. At [[DecipherCon 2000]] the group built Sokol's Day 3 Dark list overnight, Sokol won the World Championship, and four of them won Sunday's team constructed event.<ref name="sokol-dt">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-11-sokols-dcon-2000-reportd1327/ sokols-dcon-2000-report], Matt Sokol, Decktech (11 October 2000)</ref><ref name="hof-sokol">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/community/awards/ Awards and Hall of Fame], Players Committee (Matt Sokol, enshrined 27 April 2019)</ref>

== Origin ==

[[Brian Terwilliger]] said he and [[Chris Terwilliger]] found a shop in a dingy mall while moving toward the Albany region, met [[Jonny Chu]] there, and that Chu traded Brian an [[IG-2000]] for an [[Avenger]] and told them about weekly events. A few months later they joined [[Matt Sokol]], [[Aaron Kingery]], and [[Mike d'Amboise]] in the Capital Region.<ref name="clone1">[https://media.swccgstore.com/2018/09/03/the-voice-of-the-force-interview-with-swccg-documentary-directors/ The Voice of the Force: Interview with SWCCG Documentary Directors], Clone 1 with Brian Terwilliger and Brandon Baity, SWCCG Store (3 September 2018). "We randomly stumbled upon a shop in a dingy mall and met a guy name Johnny Chu (he traded me an IG-2000 for my Avenger; lol). He told us about a group of players who had events weekly. A few months later we moved to the Capital Region and joined the likes of Matt Sokol, Aaron Kingery and Mike D’amboise… ‘Team Albany’ was born."</ref>
He also said the local store at one time had five of the top twenty world-ranked players, and that Albany Yavin 4 mains and [[Hunt Down And Destroy The Jedi|Hunt Down]] were staples.<ref name="clone1" />

[[Marty Terwilliger]] (Marty Twigg) flew with Sokol and the Terwilligers, and printed the red McDonald's shirts with "Team Albany" on the front. Sokol's brother Dan Sokol missed the convention ("School and money"). Hayes Hunter sat with them as a friend while decks were built; Sokol does not list him as Albany.<ref name="sokol-dt" />

The Players Committee Hall of Fame entry for Chu says he was a long-standing member "who at one time had four of the highest-ranking Star Wars players in the world, all playing in the same store," and that he authored the Light list his teammate used to win the 2000 World Championships.<ref name="hof-chu">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/community/awards/ Awards and Hall of Fame], Players Committee (Jonny Chu, enshrined 10 August 2013)</ref>

== DecipherCon 2000 ==

Sokol finished 36th on Day 1, then Day 2 on Chu's X-wing Hidden Base and "The Beast" ([[Bring Him Before Me / Take Your Father's Place|Bring Him Before Me]] with Responsibility Of Command). Chu was disqualified Day 1 at 5–2 for a deck-list error. Chris Terwilliger finished 18th on Day 1 and reached Day 2; Yannick Lapointe beat him in the last Day 2 game for a Day 3 seat.<ref name="sokol-dt" />

Overnight before Day 3, Art, Aaron, and Brian built Sokol an [[ISB Operations / Empire's Sinister Agents|ISB Operations]] list from Kim Caton's old ISB. Sokol went to sleep at 4 a.m. and asked them to finish the lists. He beat Lapointe in the Final Confrontation.<ref name="sokol-dt" /><ref name="sokol-trando">[https://web.archive.org/web/20041026224145/http://www.trandosite.mcmail.com/iv16.htm Matt Sokol interview], [[Trandosite]] (25 October 2000)</ref>

On Sunday Sokol, Chu, Brian Terwilliger, and Chris Terwilliger won the constructed team event. Brian later wrote: "Matt Sokol also took home the team championship the next day with Johnny Chu, Chris Terwilliger and myself! #TeamAlbanyNeverDies."<ref name="eltwigg">[https://x.com/swccg/status/1327607833836331009 Brian Terwilliger quoted by @swccg], 14 November 2020</ref>

Sokol told Trandosite that winning the team tournament was the other highlight of the weekend after the World Finals: "team albany has been trying to do something like that for a while....and to win as a team felt great."<ref name="sokol-trando" />

Brian later said the 2000 team title would always be his favorite, even though 2014 Worlds runner-up was his best solo result.<ref name="clone1" />

== Later ==

At the [[2014 World Championship]] in Toronto, Brian Terwilliger finished runner-up. The Top 8 also included Chris Terwilliger (seed 5) and Aaron Kingery (seed 8); Sokol was seed 3. A forum post that weekend read "Good job Team Albany!!!"<ref name="worlds-2014">[[2014 World Championship]]</ref>

Brian posted the tribute video ''TAWND - Team Albany Will Never Die'' on 27 May 2021.<ref name="tawnd">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SkDblhdtyq8 TAWND - Team Albany Will Never Die], Brian Terwilliger (27 May 2021). Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-SkDblhdtyq8 Internet Archive].</ref>

Chu later also played with [[Kashyyyk Train of Dominance]].
